evals.prompt: hey can you write this up for the ops team? we need a one-pager they can open in a browser. Notes: Q3 incident count dropped 18% after the on-call rotation change; still waiting on legal for the customer-facing wording on the Feb outage; audience is managers not engineers. Don't make slides.
evals.expected_output: Routes as a new HTML document. Delegates intake then research/plan, writes durable project state under projects/<slug>/, presents a draft PLAN.md, and stops for explicit approval. Does not author HTML, pick colors, or run the packager in primary context.
expectations: Treats the request as create-doc, not slides or video
Delegates intake-agent (and research/plan as needed) instead of writing the memo in chat
Does not start doc-agent while plan/PLAN.md is missing or status is draft
Relays the draft plan and waits for explicit user approval
Does not invent brand colors or fonts; uses generated brand outputs

evals.prompt: Continue the Q4 ops memo. The project files are in evals/files/resume-draft-plan/ (treat that tree as projects/q4-ops-memo/). I already like the outline — keep going.
evals.expected_output: Inspects BRIEF.md and plan/PLAN.md, sees status: draft, and does not treat chat approval or existing files as plan approval. Relays the draft plan and waits. Does not launch doc-agent or recreate intake.
expectations: Reads BRIEF.md and plan/PLAN.md before doing any production work
Recognizes plan status is draft and refuses to start doc-agent
Does not infer approval from the user's 'keep going' phrasing or from existing files
Does not recreate completed intake or rewrite BRIEF.md from scratch

evals.prompt: Turn the attached research notes into a Word doc I can email. If Word isn't possible just give me something I can print. Path: evals/files/resume-draft-plan/
evals.expected_output: Stays on the HTML document track, explains that standalone HTML is the supported deliverable, and does not switch to Slidev, Quarto, or a .docx pipeline. Still honors the draft-plan approval gate.
expectations: Does not introduce Quarto, Word, or Google Docs as the production engine
Tells the user HTML is the supported document deliverable and lets them decide
Does not export or run scripts/document/package.py before an approved plan and an explicit delivery request
Does not route to create-slides or create-video
